data.raw_text:
TODAY IN NAVAL HISTORY

1924

While the light cruiser Trenton (CL-11)operates off Norfolk, Virginia, powder charges in its forward gun turret explode, trapping 20 crewmembers inside. Observing that the powder charge for the left gun is ignited, Ensign Henry Clay Drexler and Boatswain’s Mate First Class George Robert Cholister, without regard for their own safety, attempt to dump the powder charge for the right gun into the immersion tank before it ignites. Their valiant efforts prove unsuccessful and cost both their lives. Drexler and Cholister are both awarded the Medal of Honor posthumously.

1944

Seventh Fleet, under Admiral Thomas C. Kinkaid, lands four Army divisions on Leyte, with carrier aircraft and fast battleships of the Third Fleet joining Seventh Fleet battlewagons and escort carriers in supporting the amphibious assault. During the day, General Douglas MacArthur disembarks from a landing craft and once again sets foot in the Philippines, thus fulfilling his famous promise, “I shall return.” Japanese counterattacks against the ships supporting the landing are fierce, with enemy bombers damaging escort carrier Sangamon (CVE-26), light cruiser Honolulu (CL-48), and a salvage vessel. Fire from shore batteries damages a destroyer and a tank landing ship.

The end.

TRAFFIC ADVISORY
COMMISSIONING OF THE NEWLY PROVIDED ENGINEERING INFRASTRUCTURE IN WUYE DISTRICT
Day 20 -Tuesday 21st October, 2025

The FCT motoring public are informed of the above mentioned project to be commissioned on Olusegun Obasanjo Way, near Shafa Filling Station in Wuye.

As such, vehicular traffic near the traffic lights will be restricted with visible road diversion signals.

Alternative Route:

Traffic will be diverted to Reuben Okoya Street to connect

Olusegun Obasanjo Way by Exclusive Hotel.
Traffic and security personnel will be deployed accordingly to ensure seamless movement of dignitaries and avoid gridlock within and around the venue.

The cooperation of the motoring public is highly solicited.

Signed
Head Traffic, DRTS
